Class EventBus

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.events.EventBus
public final class EventBus extends Object
Delivers each event it is given to the subscribers of the event's class and of all its supertypes. 
EventBus bus = EventBus.create();
bus.subscribe(OrderPlaced.class, order -> ship(order));
bus.register(new OrderListener());
bus.publish(new OrderPlaced(42));

An event reaches each subscription once, the subscribers of a type before those of its supertypes, and those of one type in the order they were subscribed. The supertypes of a class come after it, a type always before its own supertypes and Object last; among types that are not supertypes of one another, the superclass comes before the interfaces.

A bus built without an executor delivers each event on the thread that publishes it, before publish(Object) returns. An event published from a subscriber of the same bus is queued for that thread, and delivered once the event being delivered has reached all its subscribers: the events then arrive in the order they were published. A bus with an executor hands it one task per event, which delivers the event to its subscribers in order; separate events may be delivered concurrently.

A method with a subscribing annotation gets its events through the executor of the annotation instead: the delivery hands that executor a task that calls the method, and goes on to the other subscribers without waiting for it. The tasks are handed over in the order the events are delivered; whether they run in that order depends on the executor. A task does not call the method if its subscription was closed meanwhile.

An exception thrown by a subscriber goes to the exception handler, and the event goes on to its other subscribers. So does an exception thrown by the executor of a subscribing annotation when it is handed a task, such as a RejectedExecutionException. By default, the handler logs the exception at System.Logger.Level.ERROR with System.Logger. An Error is not caught, nor is an exception thrown by the handler: it propagates from the delivery, and the events queued meanwhile on the thread are dropped.

A bus is thread-safe. Subscribers can be added and removed while events are delivered: each delivery goes to the subscribers a type had when the delivery reached it.

    • register

      public Subscription register(Object listener)
      Subscribes the @Subscribe methods of a listener, those of its class and of the classes it extends, through the code gaia-events-processor generated for each of these classes. That code is found with ServiceLoader, from the class loader of each class, or from its module layer if it is in a named module: such a module declares the generated classes with provides, as the register-services goal of gaia-maven-plugin adds.

      The methods with a subscribing annotation are subscribed too. The first time the bus registers such a method, it creates the executor the annotation names, unless it was built with one for the annotation; an exception thrown meanwhile propagates, and subscribes nothing.

      The methods of a superclass are subscribed before those of its subclasses, and those of one class in the order they are declared. A method that overrides a @Subscribe method, or one with a subscribing annotation, receives its events, without the annotation.

      Parameters:
      listener - the listener
      Returns:
      the subscription of all its methods, which unsubscribes them when closed
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if neither the class of the listener nor any class it extends has generated code: none has @Subscribe methods, or none was compiled with gaia-events-processor
